history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the generic 'Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple [Nizamabad]' best matches the famous Dharmapuri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple - which is NOT in Nizamabad at all. It stands on the banks of the Godavari at Dharmapuri, about 30 km from the Jagtial district HQ, in Jagtial district, Telangana. Identity certainty: HIGH - Dharmapuri is the well-known Lakshmi Narasimha shrine of the region and one of the Nava Narasimha Kshetras. The temple was founded by king Dharma Varma (the town's name derives from his); Dharmapuri is called 'Dakshina Kashi' and the 'Banaras of South India'. The main mandapa has 48 pillars sculpted with Puranic narratives (Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, dancing Shiva). The village's older name Dharmavura/Dharmapuramu appears in the 945 CE Kurkiyala inscription of Jinavallabha. Custom: devotees first pray to the Yama idol at the entrance, then to Anjaneya, the Kshetra Swamy. Documented with the corrected town and district.

town_description: Dharmapuri is an ancient temple town on the banks of the Godavari in Jagtial district, about 30 km from Jagtial and 42 km from Mancherial. Known as 'Dakshina Kashi' / the 'Banaras of South India', it has several ancient temples, the Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy temple being the most prominent. The Godavari riverfront and the Nava Narasimha Kshetra status make it a major pilgrimage centre.
